figures.caption: Fig. 1. Workflow of the interpretable machine-learning framework, from SCADA acquisition through model benchmarking and multi-design validation, cross-model SHAP interpretability, manifold-constrained feasibility sampling and conditional-rate window derivation, to the three independent validations and the resulting operating protocol. Follow the numbered stages left to right and top to bottom; the three purple boxes are independent checks on the result, and the green bar is the operating protocol they support. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

Fig. 2. (A) Time series and (B) distribution of the input and output features of the MBR mainstream (1) before and (2) after normalization. Input features are in blue; output features are in red. The upper row is the raw time series and the lower row the same variables after standardisation; comparing them shows that scaling changes magnitude but not shape. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

figures.caption: Fig. 3. Relationship of the input and output features of the MBR mainstream (A) before and (B) after normalization. Each cell is a pairwise Pearson correlation, so darker cells mark the variable pairs that move together; comparing the two panels shows that standardisation leaves those relationships unchanged.

Fig. 4. (A) Test R2 heatmap of all 16 models and predicted vs. actual scatter plot of the Extra Tree model across three target variables: (B1) TMP, (B2) permeate flow, and (B3) membrane tank water level. Blue indicates low R2 values, and red indicates high R2 values in the heatmap. Scatter colour indicates residual magnitude; the dashed line represents perfect prediction; shaded bands indicate ±5% and ± 10% error tolerance. In the heatmap each cell is one model-target combination and redder is more accurate; in the scatter panels points should fall on the dashed 1:1 line, and the shaded bands are the 5% and 10% error tolerances. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

figures.caption: Fig. 5. (A) Model performance comparison, (B) Prediction quality, (C) Residual plot, (D) Error distribution analysis of the best-performing model (Extra Trees) on the independent validation dataset. Points on the 1:1 line and residuals scattered evenly about zero indicate that the model transfers to the independent stream without systematic bias.

Fig. 6. (A) SHAP features importance comparison heatmaps and (B) Beeswarm plot across all 16 models for (1) TMP, (2) permeate flow, and (3) water level prediction. Cell values indicate mean |SHAP| for each model–feature pair. In the heatmaps each row is a model and each column a variable, so a column that is dark across every row marks a driver all 16 models agree on; in the beeswarm plots each point is one observation, its horizontal position the effect on the prediction and its colour the value of that variable.

Fig. 7. Feasible region and measured plant performance for each of the seven inputs. Of the 500,000 sampled operating states, 207,238 (41.4%) satisfy all three performance targets simultaneously; the blue curve is a Gaussian kernel density estimate of their distribution, fitted to a random subsample of 15,000 of those states. The red step function is the measured attainment rate of the logged plant record, drawn across the true extent of each decile bin because the deciles differ widely in width, with the highest-attainment decile marked in dark red. The green band is the recommended operating zone of Table 4, which coincides with that decile by construction. Feasible-point density and attainment rate are distinct quantities and need not peak together: the density indicates where the plant has spent its operating time, whereas the rate indicates how often the three targets were met there. The recommended zone follows the rate. The blue curve shows where the plant can operate, the red step how often it met its targets there, and the green band is the recommendation, which follows the red step and not the blue curve. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

figures.caption: Fig. 8. Probability of meeting all three performance targets across every pair of operating variables, estimated from the manifold-constrained sample. Colour is the conditional feasibility rate p(all three targets met) within each bin, green indicating a high probability and red a low one; bins containing fewer than 20 sampled states are left grey. The dark green line is the 80% contour. The two navy dashed strips are the recommended bands for the variables on the two axes, taken from Table 4, and the outlined rectangle where they cross is the region satisfying both; the feasibility rate achieved inside it, computed over all sampled states it contains rather than bin by bin, is given above each panel. The crossing point of the two bands should sit on green. It does so in 20 of the 21 pairs; the single exception, HRT against SRT, identifies an interaction discussed in the text. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

figures.caption: Fig. 9. Predicted output response across the manifold-constrained feasible region. (A) Effect of SRT on water level and TMP, (B) HRT on permeate flow and TMP, (C) opposing effects of aeration rate on flow and TMP, (D) non-monotonic effect of MLSS on TMP and water level, (E) F/M on water level and flow, (F) glucose dosing rate on water level and flow. Each panel shows how two predicted outputs respond as one input varies across its full range; the dotted horizontal lines are the performance limits, so a curve crossing them marks where that target fails, and the shaded band is the recommended operating zone.

Fig. 10. Agreement between the model-derived conditional feasibility rate (blue) and the plant's measured target-attainment rate (red) across deciles of each of the seven inputs, with the paired comparison across all 70 operating bins shown in the final panel. The blue and red curves should lie on top of one another if the model reproduces plant behaviour, and in the final panel every point should fall on the dashed 1:1 line. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

Fig. 11. Recommended operating window and its validation. (A) Percentage of real logged hours meeting all three performance targets inside and outside each recommended band. (B) Attainment across all held-out hours and inside the operating window learned on months 1–7 and evaluated on months 8–11. In panel A, a longer green bar than grey bar means the recommended band outperforms the rest of the record; in panel B the right-hand bar is the attainment achieved in months the analysis never saw. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)
